clue.text: Maximum gettable for beginners on an exam

indicators.note: a beginner is where something starts, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: the opening letter of gettable
re means on, as in on the subject of
taken as written
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A student wonders what the top mark is that a beginner could hope to score on an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the crossword's usual word for 'on' or 'about'. In this boxing-themed grid, The Greatest was Muhammad Ali's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Maximum as an adjective means the largest possible, which is exactly what the superlative of great expresses.

clue.text: The Lady of Seville is taking off from a certain terminal

indicators.note: a plane taking off goes upward, and in a down entry going upward means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: la doña is Spanish for the lady, and Seville is in Spain

explanation.surface: A Spanish lady is flying out of an airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface terminal is at an airport; the real one is electrical. The tilde on doña is ignored, as accents always are in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodal describes something relating to or coming from the anode, the positive electrode of a battery or cell.

clue.text: Given the No. 1 carriage?

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of the Irish goalkeeper surnamed Given, who wore the number 1 shirt
second meaning: a light horse-drawn carriage, also called a chaise

explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' reads like a verb, but it is a surname: Shay Given kept goal for Newcastle and Ireland, and a goalkeeper wears No. 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Shay is a dialect form of chaise, an open two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle; the footballer's first name is spelt the same.

clue.text: Possibly writing small piece about one of us?

indicators.note: about means around, so one part is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: a bit is a small piece
writing is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: Perhaps a short article written about one of the paper's own readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs of basic schooling are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic, so any one of them can be clued as R. 'Us' is the readers of a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Independent is a British paper, so one of its readers, one of us, is informally a Briton.

clue.text: Suspiciously letting one off ain’t him

definitions.text: Suspiciously letting one off ain’t him

indicators.note: letting something off means releasing it, so a letter is dropped from the group
something done suspiciously is shifty, so the letters are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I, here the letter that is let go
the letters as printed, with apostrophe and space ignored

explanation.surface: Someone shiftily insists the gunman who let off a shot was not this man.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one I from AINTHIM leaves ANTHIM to rearrange. Read whole, the clue also describes a hired killer firing a round. Thomas Hearns was the boxer nicknamed the Hitman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired professional killer suspiciously letting off a round is exactly the figure the whole clue paints.

clue.text: Tediously continue playing pantomime dame?

blocks.note: first meaning: to go on for far too long
second meaning: a man playing the dame is in women's clothing, and he is on stage

explanation.walkthrough: The pantomime dame is a traditional British Christmas-show role, a comic older woman always played by a man in women's dress, so the actor is in drag and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag on is the phrasal verb for lasting tediously long; read as two words it describes a performer cross-dressed and onstage.

clue.text: Low-down type initiated contacts with former mistress? Nob

indicators.note: to initiate is to start something off, so just the starting letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the low-down is information, which in British slang is the gen
the starting letter of type
leman is an old word for a lover or mistress

explanation.surface: A lowlife gets back in touch with an old flame, and the clue adds a sneering verdict on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-down type' wants to be one villain; it splits into GEN plus the T of type. Gentleman Jim was the boxer James J. Corbett, and 20 Down is JIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A nob is British slang for a person of high social rank, and a gentleman is a man of good family.

clue.text: Quality of the Lions timelessly remains in the memory

indicators.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time, so without time means that letter is dropped
one thing sitting inside another is held within it

blocks.note: the word the with its T taken away
ROM is read-only memory in a computer
remains in the sense of still exists, which is what is says

explanation.surface: The courage of the British and Irish Lions rugby team lives on in fans' memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks as if it belongs to 'the Lions', but it is wordplay: the HE comes from it, though the definition also claims the Lions. Lions here are brave people generally.
explanation.definitionFit: Lions stand for courage, and the quality that lion-hearted people show is bravery of the highest kind.

clue.text: Compère will need this guy before November

blocks.note: first meaning: a host on stage needs a microphone
second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the M word comes just before the N word, November

explanation.walkthrough: November is the code word for N, not a month, and the word for M is also a man's name, hence 'guy'. Iron Mike was Mike Tyson's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A mike is the informal short form of microphone, and also the radio code word for the letter M.

clue.text: A high-quality tea Mark’s passed up in Coloradan town

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving up means travelling to the top, so the letter goes from the bottom to the start

blocks.note: a and an are the same article
Assam is a fine black tea from north-east India
M is short for mark; it names the final letter of the tea, the one that moves

explanation.surface: A fine cup of tea has been carried up and served in a small Colorado town.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the abbreviation for mark, and the M at the foot of ANASSAM is moved to the top. Manassa is the birthplace of Jack Dempsey, the Manassa Mauler (27 Down).
explanation.definitionFit: Manassa is a small town in Conejos County in southern Colorado, so it is a place in that US state.

clue.text: When you might need New Year diary for resolution? Separate answers in it

indicators.note: a resolution resolves something into a different form, so the letters are worked out into a fresh order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Y is the abbreviation for year
taken as written
A is short for answer, and two of them go in separately

explanation.surface: A new diary is bought for writing down New Year resolutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' sounds like a New Year promise, but it is the anagram signal. The definition is the gap in the saying: you save something for a rainy day.
explanation.definitionFit: Money is put aside for a rainy day, the idiom for a future time of hardship when you might need it.

clue.text: A city of Russia to one of Belarus, in deserts

indicators.note: to desert is to abandon, so the named letters walk out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
Minsk, the capital of Belarus, once the letters of in have left it

explanation.surface: A journey is described from a Russian city to a Belarusian one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a preposition placing something, but it is the pair of letters that leaves MINSK.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomsk is a large university city in western Siberia, so it is one of the cities of Russia.

clue.text: Superb, quiet retreats are almost devoid of basics for living

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word is read backwards
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: ace means excellent
a lull is a quiet spell
are without its last letter

explanation.surface: Fine, peaceful retreats are nearly bare of life's essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' looks like a noun for quiet getaways; it is a verb turning the quiet word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cells are the basic units of living things, so something acellular lacks them, like a virus.

clue.text: Tolerated a shorter version of the Ancient Mariner?

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

blocks.clueFragment: a shorter version of the Ancient
blocks.note: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner is a long poem; a short lyric poem is an ode

explanation.surface: Someone put up with an abridged edition of Coleridge's famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The title splits in two: the mariner is a sailor, and the poem shrinks to a shorter kind of poem. The question mark flags this loose reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Abode is an old past tense of abide, and to abide something is to bear or put up with it.

clue.text: Deer series being talked about

indicators.note: something being talked about is spoken, so it is the sound of the word that counts

blocks.note: a series of things in a line is a row

explanation.surface: A wildlife documentary series about deer is the talk of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Row, as in a line of seats, and the small deer's name are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe is a small European species of deer, so the word names a kind of deer.

clue.text: Worked through “U”?

blocks.note: first meaning: finished, as a task completed
second meaning: socially proper

explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and non-upper-class British usage, so U means socially acceptable, the done thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Done means completed, and also conventionally proper in polite society, which is what U denoted.

clue.text: Tale with a twist in does perhaps factor in ruin?

indicators.note: a twist changes the shape of something, so its letters are rearranged
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a tale is a story
does, female deer, are examples of deer

explanation.surface: A story with a plot twist turns on a factor in someone's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe, and 'perhaps' marks them as an example of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is whatever brings something to ruin, so it is the agent or factor responsible for the wreckage.

clue.text: Here in board meeting a knight starts to stiffen

definitions.text: Here in board meeting a knight starts

blocks.clueFragment: Here in board meeting a knight starts
blocks.note: first meaning: on a chessboard, a white knight starts on square b1, read as letter plus number word
second meaning: to reinforce a garment such as a corset with whalebone stays

explanation.surface: At a board meeting a knight of the realm starts to get rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' sounds like a company meeting, but the board is a chessboard and the place is the knight's starting square, written in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsets were once stiffened with strips of whalebone, so to bone a garment is to make it rigid.

clue.text: Supporting vineyards, woman who’s operating the presses?

indicators.note: in a down entry a support holds something up from below, so the next piece goes underneath

blocks.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine; crus is the plural
her stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman who backs the vineyards runs the wine presses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface woman runs the presses; in the wordplay she is only the word HER under the vineyards. Bonecrusher was the nickname of the boxer James Smith, with 17 Across BONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something pressing grapes squashes them, and one who squashes things is by definition the one who crushes.

clue.text: Thumbs up, Badenoch predominantly struck dumb

indicators.note: pre-dominant read as coming before the rest, so the leading letter is the one used
something struck off a list is removed, so that letter is taken out
things that are churned up are disturbed out of order, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: thumbs with its B removed
the leading letter of Badenoch, the letter that is struck

explanation.surface: Kemi Badenoch, the Conservative leader, gives a thumbs-up but is left speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thumbs up' wants to be a gesture; 'up' is the mixing signal. Kemi Badenoch is a British Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtum is British slang from Yiddish for silent, so to keep shtum is to stay dumb, saying nothing.

clue.text: Were he thematic, this GI would be Smokin’

definitions.text: Were he thematic, this GI would be Smokin’

blocks.clueFragment: Were he thematic, this GI would be Smokin’
blocks.note: surface reading: an American soldier who might be lighting up a cigarette
setter's reading: a US soldier is a GI plus a common first name

explanation.surface: If this American soldier fitted the theme, he would be the smoker of the boxing world.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is buried mid-clue: GI and the answer together make the toy soldier's name, and the boxer Frazier was Smokin' plus the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A G.I. Joe is the generic American soldier, and Smokin' Joe Frazier beat Ali in 1971, fitting the boxing theme.

clue.text: Caught working out the little fella

indicators.note: if you catch what someone says you hear it, so it is the sound that matters

blocks.note: people work out at a gym

explanation.surface: The small man was spotted exercising at the fitness centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like a cricket dismissal or being found out; here it means heard. Gentleman Jim (7 Down) was the boxer James J. Corbett.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim is the short form, a diminutive, of the name James, so it is a little name for a fellow.

clue.text: My sweet pasta sauce is on the counter

indicators.note: counter means against or opposite, so the direction of reading is turned around

blocks.note: ragu is an Italian meat sauce for pasta
the 's of a contraction stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone tells their darling that the jar of pasta sauce is out on the kitchen worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' is a kitchen surface in the picture and a turnaround signal in the wordplay. Sugar Ray Robinson and Sugar Ray Leonard were both boxers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is a term of endearment, like honey or sweetheart, that someone might call a loved one.

clue.text: Top sides rev Bellamy’s team up?

blocks.note: to gun an engine is to rev it hard
Craig Bellamy played for and later coached the Wales national football team

explanation.surface: A fan asks whether the Welsh football side is about to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rev ... up' reads as one phrasal verb, but only 'rev' is used. Gunwale is pronounced gunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwales are the upper edges along a boat's sides, the rails at the top of each side.

clue.text: Keen customer might need this to access her online bank details?

blocks.note: a customer holds an account, abbreviated a/c

blocks.clueFragment: to access her online bank details
blocks.note: logging in to a bank needs proof of identity, ID

explanation.surface: An eager shopper needs this to log in to her online banking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen customer' wants to be one phrase for an enthusiastic buyer; 'Keen' stands alone as the definition. An account number plus ID is what a bank login asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and acid are both used for something sharp or cutting, as in a keen edge or an acid tongue.

clue.text: On retirement, right to join top club

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so everything is read from the end
joining a group means getting in among its members, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the top spot is number one, written NO I
R is short for right

explanation.surface: On retiring, a right-winger is allowed to join an exclusive club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top club' looks like a smart members' club; the definition is the golf sense. Iron Mike was Mike Tyson's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a golf club with a flat-faced metal head, one of the standard clubs in a golfer's bag.

clue.text: Meat Loaf’s formula? Uplifting record taking chap to top

indicators.note: lifting up in a down entry means reading from the bottom upward

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
the person who tops a cake with frosting

explanation.surface: The singer Meat Loaf's secret to success is a rousing record that sends a guy to number one.
explanation.walkthrough: Meat Loaf looks like the rock singer; read as two words, it is the dish. The question mark warns of this.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is the set of instructions and ingredients for making a dish, such as a meat loaf.

clue.text: Films refuse to spread viral phenomena

indicators.note: something spread out stretches around, so one piece covers the other

blocks.note: memes are online jokes or images that go viral
bran is husk, the refuse left from sifting grain

explanation.surface: Movie studios decline to share internet craze clips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' looks like movies and 'refuse' like a verb; one is the definition and the other is the noun for waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A membrane is a thin pliable layer of tissue or material, which is one sense of the word film.

clue.text: Hand 7 addressed boxes a year from Christmas

indicators.note: taking one thing from another means subtracting it
a box encloses things, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: 7 Down is a gentleman, who is addressed as Mr
taken as written
Yule is Christmas, with its Y taken away
Y is short for year, the letter removed from Christmas

explanation.surface: A man hands over boxed presents a year after Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' looks like a verb but is a noun. 'boxes' also nods to the theme: Jack Dempsey was the Manassa Mauler.
explanation.definitionFit: A mauler is slang for a hand, especially a big rough one, since hands are what maul things.

clue.text: He’s out of the way in Paris flat

indicators.note: being out of something means gone from it, so those letters leave

blocks.note: the word the with its H and E gone
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A man has left a Paris street for an apartment there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a Paris apartment; it is the adjective. 'He's' tells you which letters go: HE is out of THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A true surface is exactly level and even, so a carpenter would call a perfectly level board true.

clue.text: Rough, with the shakes

blocks.note: first meaning: full of rocks, rugged
second meaning: unsteady, wobbly

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses can describe a bad patch, which hides the split. Rocky Marciano was the unbeaten heavyweight, and Rocky the film boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky describes rugged stony ground and also something unstable or shaky, like a rocky table.

clue.text: Three-foot garden

blocks.note: first meaning: a unit of length equal to three feet
second meaning: the American word for a garden

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes it sound like a tiny garden; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard measures three feet, and in American usage the yard is the grassy plot round a house.

clue.text: Theatre actor in the end eschewing training under Larry

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is taken
to eschew is to shun or avoid, so the letter is left out
training puts something into a new shape, so the letters are reformed

blocks.note: the final letter of actor
the letters of under Larry with one R taken out

explanation.surface: An actor skipped drama school but learnt on the job under Larry Olivier.
explanation.walkthrough: Larry looks like Laurence Olivier, but is just letters. The Theatre Royal, Drury Lane is a historic London West End theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Drury Lane is the familiar name of the Theatre Royal in London's Covent Garden, so it names a theatre.

clue.text: Brought up Talk Radio’s secret

indicators.note: bringing something up in a down entry means it now reads from the bottom upward

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Someone has raised a secret on a talk radio phone-in.
explanation.walkthrough: Talk Radio is a British speech station, but its name is only the letters that hold the answer, read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something dark is the idiom for keeping it hidden, so dark means secret or concealed.

clue.text: Western capital in which you’ll find an appropriate leader

indicators.note: heading west in an across entry means going right to left, against the reading direction
finding something inside another means one holds the other

blocks.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
an as in five pounds an hour means per

explanation.surface: A Western capital city is where you'd find a fitting ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western capital' looks like one city in the West; 'Western' is the turnaround. 'appropriate' because Rome is the city of emperors.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme ruler of an empire, and ancient Rome's rulers held that title, making it fitting.

clue.text: Pounds sterling this job will make student!

indicators.note: if one piece plus another makes a whole, the whole minus that piece leaves the other

blocks.note: L, from the Latin libra on the pound sign, is the letter taken away
a student is a learner, here with its first letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone declares that this job will pay enough to fund a student.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle: pound (L) plus the answer makes LEARNER. A nice little earner is British slang for a lucrative job.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner, in British slang, is a job or scheme that brings in money, as in a nice little earner.
